rationale:
Evidence: iteration 6 (score 69.30, the best verified design) uses the 7-sensor array at x = -0.075 to 0.075 (0.025 m spacing), y 0.06, footprint 0.016, mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.12, base_speed 1.0, kp 7.0, kd 0.3, ki 0.02, last_direction. Oval progress rose from 0.137 (kp 5.5) to 0.242 (kp 7.0). The s-bend (0.14) and slalom (0.10) were flat. max_error sits near 0.06 on every track, and rms_error is 0.024 to 0.031.

What I accepted from the critique: (1) The kp 8.5 step was too large. At kp 8.5, any signal above about 0.69 drives the inside wheel's command negative, so the wheel reverses on bends. Linear extrapolation of steering_oscillation from kp 5.5 to 7.0 also puts kp 8.5 near 0.25, leaving almost no margin. (2) The kd-to-kp ratio falls as kp rises, so I want a smaller step. (3) The revision's kd 0.4 and ki 0.0 were not the raced-best values (kd 0.3, ki 0.02), so that design was not a one-variable change. I restore kd 0.3 and ki 0.02.

What I rejected: the claim that the drift is curvature-limited is kept as a hypothesis, not a finding. Its rejection test is max_error staying at 0.060 or more with progress unchanged. Speed stays at 1.0 because changing it now would confound the gain test.

What I changed: kp 7.0 to 8.0 (+14 percent), with everything else equal to the raced best. This is the only difference from iteration 6. It limits the saturation region to signals above about 0.84 and keeps oscillation nearer 0.22.

Predictions (guesses): oval progress rises by at least 0.02 to about 0.26; s-bend and slalom stay near 0.14 and 0.10; steering_oscillation stays under 0.25; slalom line_loss_events stay at 1 or fall.

Decision rule, per track: if oval progress rises by at least 0.02 on the seed mean and steering_oscillation is under 0.25, continue kp toward 9 in the next step. If steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.3, hold kp and raise kd in one step. If s-bend and slalom progress are still 0.14 and 0.10, the next test should change the start or the line-loss rule, not the gains. Completion within 3 s is out of reach at speed 1.0, so this race is a stability and progress test.
